_comment: Stegosaurus stenops, built to the game's 8.5 m (sim.c). Proportions are rounded from Maidment et al. (2015, PLoS ONE 10: e0138352) on NHMUK PV R36730 ('Sophie') and Scott Hartman's skeletal: graviportal legs with a long femur over a short shin (tibia about 0.6 of the femur) and a very short foot, forelimbs much shorter than the hind (humerus about 0.6 of the femur) so the back arches high over the hips and the head is carried low, a tiny narrow skull, a short neck, a deep narrow body, and the tail level and stiff.

Seventeen alternating plates run in two rows from the neck to the tail, tallest over the hips and the tail base (Gilmore 1914; Carpenter 1998), and four spikes stand out sideways and up at the tail end (the thagomizer). All lengths are fractions of the body length along the spine.
